title: HTTP 5xx provider outages are not mapped to serviceUnavailable

evidence.quote:
default:
            let errorMessage = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8) ?? "Unknown error"
            throw AIServiceError.networkError(errorMessage)

reasoning: The domain error model distinguishes provider unavailability, but OpenAIService maps every non-401/non-429 failure, including 500, 502, 503, and 504 responses, to networkError with the raw response body. That makes transient provider outages indistinguishable from request/client failures and prevents callers from applying outage-specific retry or user messaging behavior.
reproduction: Return HTTP 503 from the OpenAI-compatible endpoint. summarize throws AIServiceError.networkError(...) rather than AIServiceError.serviceUnavailable.
recommendation: Map 500...599, or at least 503/504, to AIServiceError.serviceUnavailable. Keep networkError for transport failures or unmapped status codes where the body is useful.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests do not exercise any HTTP status mapping because they do not use an injected session or mock network responses.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add mocked response tests for 503 and assert AIServiceError.serviceUnavailable; optionally cover 500, 502, and 504 consistently.
minimumFixScope: Modules/AIServices/Sources/AIServices/Services/OpenAIService.swift: extend the status-code switch in summarize and add focused status-mapping tests.
